title: Duplicate WIZNET5K driver/library files in MicroPython tree
body:
I noticed that the wiznet5k files are duplicated in the tree. As far as I can see, the one located in lib/wiznet5k are the latest and "linked" to WIZNET development branch (i.e. [wiznet5k @ 0803fc5]), whereas a similar set of files is located in drivers/wiznet5k and seems very old :
Original source: https://github.com/Wiznet/W5500_EVB/tree/master/ioLibrary Taken on: 30 August 2014
Shall not this older version of files be removed, making sure that some builds which could be dependent on these can use the newer ones instead?

Apparently, the only port relying on this old version is stm32. Can anyone try to use lib/wiznet5k instead of drivers/wiznet5k in ports/stm32/Makefile and ports/stm32/network_wiznet5k.c files? I have no STM32 platform to test.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: It does not even compile. Fixing the Makefile was the easy part. But then are some compile errors compiling stm32/modnwwiznet5k.c.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Also extmod/networkl_wiznet5k.c should be use instead stm32/modnwwiznet5k.c. But that is a major change.

comments.body:
@participant1 
Which board compilation are you working on? The pybv10 (default) compiles OK for me. If I can help making your board version compile at least. I cannot test, I have no stm32 based board.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 
My Makefile block related to WIZnet contains:
```
ifneq ($(MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K),0)
WIZNET5K_DIR=lib/wiznet5k
INC += -I$(TOP)/$(WIZNET5K_DIR) -I$(TOP)/$(WIZNET5K_DIR)/Ethernet
CFLAGS_MOD += -DMICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K=$(MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K) -D_WIZCHIP_=$(MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K)
CFLAGS_MOD += -DWIZCHIP_PREFIXED_EXPORTS=1
ifeq ($(MICROPY_PY_LWIP),1)
# When using MACRAW mode (with lwIP), maximum buffer space must be used for the raw socket
CFLAGS_MOD += -DWIZCHIP_USE_MAX_BUFFER
endif
SRC_MOD += extmod/network_wiznet5k.c # modnwwiznet5k.c
SRC_MOD += $(addprefix $(WIZNET5K_DIR)/,\
	Ethernet/w$(MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K)/w$(MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K).c \
	Ethernet/wizchip_conf.c \
	Ethernet/socket.c \
	Internet/dns/dns.c \
	Internet/DHCP/dhcp.c \
	)
endif
```
The only remaining link error is `machine_spi_type`. I don't know where it's coming from.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: You have to add it in modmachine.h, just like the other declarations like e.g., as machine_i2s_type.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
This line:
`	Ethernet/w$(MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K)/w$(MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K).c \`
should be
`	Ethernet/W$(MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K)/w$(MICROPY_PY_NETWORK_WIZNET5K).c \`

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: No, it's different. machine_spi_type does not exist. It is called machine_hard_spi_type.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
So you may add to modmachine.h:
```
extern const mp_obj_type_t machine_hard_spi_type;

#define machine_spi_type machine_hard_spi_type
```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 
I added 
```
#define machine_spi_type    machine_hard_spi_type
```
to `stm32/modmachine.h` et voilà !! It compiles and links

comments.body: It seems to be a problem with every attempt trying to communicate with the W5500. The message `MPY: enabling IRQs` is in shared/runtime/pyexec.c, function pyexec_friendly_repl(). So OSError: 16 is the topic to look at,

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: The problem is, that a wrong data type is supplied for SPI  to the WIZNET driver. Then, the spi_transfer() function does not have the reference it needs, and no SPI transfer takes place.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 
I came to the same conclusion this morning, and was having a look at that. Unfortunately, I am currently on vacation and I have limited access to my computer and can't really spend a lot of time for the moment on that topic. I'll come back as soon as I can. :-)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I found the reason: It is twice a substitution.
In stm32/spi.c, line 684, the spi object is returned as self->spi, where self is the argument of the network_wiznet constructor. That is the pointer to be used in SPI transfer calls. and it is store in the wiznetwiznet5k_obj. BUT, in wiz_spi_write() machine_hard_spi_transfer() is called with that value for the transfer, and that uses <input Ptr>->spi.
machine_hard_spi_transfer() cannot be changed, 
One coulf change the function spi_from_mp_obj(), which is also used by modnwcc3k.c. That is a expired WiFi adapter.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
The actual states is here: https://github.com/participant1/micropython/tree/stm32_wizlib
A sample start script is:
```
import network
import machine, pyb
spi=machine.SPI(1)
nic = network.WIZNET5K(spi, machine.Pin("X5"), machine.Pin("X4"))
nic.active(1)
nic.ifconfig(('10.0.0.139', '255.255.255.0','10.0.0.240', '10.0.0.240'))
```
This is without LWIP. For LWIP, the pin interrupt functionality has to be added.

```
import network

spi = machine.SPI(1, baudrate=20_000_000)
nic = network.WIZNET5K(spi, machine.Pin("X5"), machine.Pin("X4"), machine.Pin("X3"))

```
